subject: Using loo::loo() when some data points have high Pareto k estimate

messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Using loo::loo() when some data points have high Pareto k estimate
parts:
Suppose that I run

    loo_obj <- loo::loo(log_lik_sample)

and find that data points i[1], ..., i[n] have Pareto k estimates >= 0.5. Following the advice in the documentation, I rerun explicit leave-one-out estimations, sampling from p(θ | y_{-i[j]}) to get improved elpd estimates and accompanying standard errors for data points i_1, ..., i_n.

How do I combine these results with the information in loo_obj to compute elpd_loo and its standard error? If I understand correctly, I can get a new elpd_loo estimate by taking loo_obj$pointwise[ , 'elpd_loo'], replacing the entries for i_1, ..., i_n, and summing the result. But how do I recompute se_elpd_loo?

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Using loo::loo() when some data points have high Pareto k estimate
parts: Hi Kevin, like you said the total elpd is the sum of the individual contributions. The standard error we use in the loo package is just sqrt(N * var(elpd)).

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Using loo::loo() when some data points have high Pareto k estimate
parts: On Thu, Feb 11, 2016 at 4:49 PM, Kevin Van Horn <ke...@ksvanhorn.com> wrote:

Jonah, when you write var(elpd), are you summing independent variances for each data point, or are you doing something else? That is, do you compute estimates and variances separately for each data point, and then combine them?
The elpds are computed one at a time in a loop (or several at a time if parallelizing) and then the variance of those elpds is computed after. Is that what you mean?
If so, could I just call loo::loo() on the log-likelihood matrix updated with draws from the leave-one-out Stan runs for the problematic data points?
I haven't done it before but I don't see why not (although maybe Aki or Andrew will think of a reason not to do it).

messages.author: a8b6459b77c849fe
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Using loo::loo() when some data points have high Pareto k estimate
parts:
On Thursday, February 11, 2016 at 3:36:17 PM UTC-7, Jonah Gabry wrote:
The elpds are computed one at a time in a loop (or several at a time if parallelizing) and then the variance of those elpds is computed after. Is that what you mean?

OK, so you did mean literally the R expression sqrt(N * var(elpd)), where elpd is the vector of pointwise elpd estimates, and I've now verified that for a loo object x and N data points,

    x$se_elpd_loo == sqrt(N * var(x$pointwise[,'elpd_loo'])).

Thanks, that clears things up.
